observations: Photo 0 shows a complete-looking engine bay/engine assembly on a stand or floor, with visible intake/exhaust plumbing, fuel/ignition components, and a serpentine belt/pulley system.
Photo 0 includes a visible alternator and multiple sensors/solenoids on the top/side of the engine.
Photo 1 shows the same engine from a different angle; alternator and crank/serpentine pulleys are visible.
No clear engine model code, engine cover text, or VIN/part number is readable in either photo.
The seller’s words mention “Hyundai kia engine 4cylinder”, but the photos do not show a readable Hyundai/Kia engine designation.

claims.evidence: Neither photo shows a readable Hyundai/Kia badge, engine code, or model/part number to confirm brand or exact 4-cylinder variant.

risks.risk: Exact engine family/model is not identifiable from the photos, so compatibility and correct replacement parts may be wrong.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine identification plate/engine code stamping (usually on block or cylinder head) and the full engine cover label if present.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an unknown 4-cylinder engine assembly with compatibility risk (worst case: may not fit or may require extra parts).

risks.risk: Unknown running condition (may be seized, low compression, oil leaks, or missing components). Photos only show appearance.
risks.proof: Video of a cold start (or at least cranking with RPM) plus a short clip showing no abnormal smoke and stable idle.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven to run (worst case: treated as not working / needs overhaul).

risks.risk: Missing or swapped accessories (e.g., alternator, sensors, brackets, hoses) that affect installation and cost.
risks.proof: Photo checklist: show all accessories included laid out (alternator, starter, sensors, coils/injectors, brackets) and confirm what is included/excluded in writing.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown inclusions (worst case: buyer may need to source missing parts).

risks.risk: Mileage/usage history and prior damage (overheating, bent valves, water ingress) cannot be confirmed remotely.
risks.proof: Compression test results and leak-down test (or at minimum, scan report for stored/freeze-frame codes).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown history (worst case: assume potential internal wear).

proof_requests: Clear close-up photos of the engine code/ID plate or stamped code on the block/head (must be readable).
Video of cold start or at least confirmed running with sound and stable idle (and no heavy smoke).
A written list of what is included with the engine (starter, alternator, injectors/coils, sensors, ECU, wiring harness, turbo if any, etc.).
Compression test (and ideally leak-down) results or a scan report showing no critical faults.
response.reason: The photos show an engine assembly but do not provide readable Hyundai/Kia identification or engine code, and the running condition is not verifiable remotely. To price safely, you need the engine code/ID and proof it runs.
